title: Malformed `Description-Content-Type` crashes with `IndexError` or is silently accepted
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

```python
from packaging import metadata
def load(dct):
    return metadata.Metadata.from_email(
        "Metadata-Version: 2.6\nName: packaging\nVersion: 1.0\n"
        f"Description-Content-Type: {dct}\n")
load("text/plain; x*")    # IndexError: string index out of range
load("text/plain; {b}")   # accepted, value kept as 'text/plain; {b}'
```
Expected for both: the usual `ExceptionGroup` holding one `metadata.InvalidMetadata` whose `field` is `"description-content-type"`. The same should happen for `text/plain; a}b`, for an unterminated quoted parameter (`text/plain; charset="unterminated`, today misreported as a charset problem) and for a folded value spread over two lines (today a raw `ValueError`). Reading `.description_content_type` from `Metadata.from_raw({...}, validate=False)` with such a value must raise `InvalidMetadata` too.

The message should include the repr of the offending value and say it "is not a valid content type", e.g. `'text/plain; x*' is not a valid content type for 'description-content-type'`. Well-formed but unsupported types such as `application/octet-stream` must still be rejected.
acceptance: `x*`, `{b}`, `a}b`, unterminated-quote and folded values give `InvalidMetadata` for `description-content-type` with the message shape above
Valid values (`text/markdown; variant=gfm`, `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`) still work and unsupported types are still rejected
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
